issue_context.title: scheduler/extender: extend the current `ExtenderFilterResult` struct to include node status
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

Updated on 13/06/2020:

- ~~[ ] update extender design proposal~~ (not possible, see https://github.com/kubernetes/community/pull/4816)
- [x] migrate it to k/enhancements https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1840
- [x] submit a API change PR https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1850
- [ ] implement it https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/92866

**What would you like to be added**:

I'd like to extend the current `ExtenderFilterResult` struct to include node status of the failed pod.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9e991415386e4cf155a24b1da15becaa390438d8/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-scheduler/extender/v1/types.go#L86-L97

e.g. 

- add a new map `FailedUnresolvableNodes` to include `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable` nodes 
- or use an extensive struct to include both status and message in the node map (which supersedes current `FailedNodes` map)

**Why is this needed**:

`FailedNodes` is a map of string to string which includes failed message only.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9e991415386e4cf155a24b1da15becaa390438d8/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-scheduler/extender/v1/types.go#L82-L83

The status of the failed node is hardcoded to `Unscheduable` here.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9e991415386e4cf155a24b1da15becaa390438d8/pkg/scheduler/core/generic_scheduler.go#L520-L526

The extender filter can't report that failed nodes are unresolvable like built-in filters.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7ba332a839c844ef4ba0191ddca2ce3601d283af/pkg/scheduler/core/generic_scheduler.go#L1034-L1047

cc @resouer @Huang-Wei
yes, when `extenders.Filter()` can return the status of the node, we must update this logic to respect the status returned by the extender.
@kubernetes/sig-scheduling-feature-requests

One thing I’m thinking about is: if we can keep current failedNodeMap struct, say still use string as the value, but set an implicit contract with extenders, and then parse the returned error string to a particular type.

If we introduce Status as the the value, extender has to depends on k/k, that sort of violates the intention to move out extender API.

To sum up, there are several options:

- **Option 1:** keep `FailedNodesMap map[string]string` as is. In the scheduler core, add additional logic to check whether the return error reason contains (or starts with, well it's an implicit contract) keyword "UnschedulableAndUnresolvable", if so, set the status to `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable`; otherwise, set it to `Unschedulable` as before. In this way, we don't need to update the extender v1 API, and also user's extenders won't be impacted.
- **Option 2:** replace `FailedNodesMap map[string]string` with `FailedNodesMap map[string]framework.Status`. This adds an extra deps to k/k, which may violate our intention of moving extender API to staging. To make the API backwards compatible, we may need extra decoding logic to ensure both plain string (old version) and framework.Status get decoded properly.
- **Option 3:** adds `FailedAndUnresolvableNodes map[string]string`. As this adds a new field, so it's API backwards compatible naturally.

On the other hand, the staging extender v1 isn't really a standard k8s version - it's just a JSON format contract negotiated with the users. We can only support one version due to missing of GVK, unless there are multiple endpoints served (which is almost impossible).

> If you agree, I can send a PR to implement it.

Thanks @cofyc. Just a reminder, for option 3, we may need to update (or migrate) existing extender KEP as it involves API changes.
I think option 3 is the one we should go with. Option 1 in my opinion shouldn't be considered at all, while option 2 breaks backward compatibility.

Thanks!

Current extender [design proposal](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/design-proposals/scheduling/scheduler_extender.md) doesn't document `preempt` verb (maybe documented in another place?). I'll update it first, then submit an API change proposal. 

We can migrate the doc to `k/enhancements` after it's done.
/assign

I think we should adhere to API versioning (and release v2) before adding more fields. Unless this is urgent.

Certainly addressing  #88634 is important, but I think they can move in parallel as long as we treat it as a versioned API.

review_comments: as a serialized API type, this file is strange... it has no json tags, etc... are the scheduler extender APIs being actively expanded?

It is not "actively" expanded per se, I think this is the first update in a very long time. This is an old API, it precedes the involvement of most active members in sig scheduling, we are aware that it misses json tags and proper versioning, there is an open issue to fix that:  #88634

would this happen?
I can only think of the case where the extender returns both states for the same Node.
yes, ignore the nodes in `failedMap` if they are already in `failedAndUnresolvableMap`
please add a comment that this only happens if the extender returns it in both

Although a little rare, do you think it's necessary to add a case to cover the path that "extender may overwrite the statuses"? i.e., the tuple `{feasibleNodes, statuses}` passed onto the extender(s) is `{[a, b], {c: Unchedulable}}`, extenders may return feasibleNodes as [a], while statuses as {c: UnschedualbeAndUnresolvable, b: Unschedulable}.

I think it's necessary. The case "extender may overwrite the statuses" is added (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/92866/files#diff-af29ae211c469a644b28df812d85bf717e76e623126ef3d5a14d07989c883fddR353). PTAL.
is it an error to include a node in FailedNodes and not in this map?

> ...and preemption would not change anything

is that what unresolveable means? the doc doesn't seem to match the variable name

> is it an error to include a node in FailedNodes and not in this map?

No. We are practically considering the union, however nodes in this map don't get considered during preemption.

> > ...and preemption would not change anything
> 
> is that what unresolveable means? the doc doesn't seem to match the variable name

Unresolvable is the term used in the scheduler pkg to indicate that preempting pods from a node doesn't make it schedulable for an incoming pod.

I see. I parsed this as "(Failed Nodes) And (Unresolveable Nodes)" instead of "(Failed And Unresolveable) Nodes". If Unresolveable implies Failed, then would it be clearer to just call this UnresolveableNodes?

this tries to mimic scheduling plugin statuses, which could be "Unschedulable" or "UnschedulableAndUnresolvable".

but I don't have a strong opinion about removing the "Failed" part
if this is following an existing pattern in this API, that's fine
